chunks: Or a treasure should have been given to him, or he should have had an orchard from which he could eat. And these wicked people say: You only follow a man ensorcelled.

key_terms.الظَّالِمُونَ: the wicked/disbelievers who oppressed the truth
key_terms.جَنَّةٌ: orchard or garden with fruit trees
key_terms.مَّسْحُورًا: ensorcelled or under the influence of magic

ai.seo_question: What did the disbelievers say about the Prophet's lack of material wealth?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the materialistic criteria of the Quraysh, who equated prophethood with worldly power and abundance, thereby dismissing Muhammad’s (peace be upon him) spiritual authority. The mention of 'magic' (masḥūr) reflects their attempt to delegitimize his eloquence and miracles as supernatural enchantment rather than divine truth. This critique underscores the recurring theme in the Quran where the elite reject prophets due to their humble origins and lack of immediate wealth.
